```{python}
#| code-fold: show
import math
import re

import torch
from torch import nn

text = open("data/shakespeare.txt").read()
chars = sorted(set(text))
n_chars = len(chars)
index = {ch: i for i, ch in enumerate(chars)}
ids = torch.tensor([index[ch] for ch in text])
n_train = 90_000
train_ids, val_ids = ids[:n_train], ids[n_train:]
seq_len = 64
batch_size = 32
lm_lr = 0.005


def decode(t):
    return "".join(chars[i] for i in t.tolist())


class CharModel(nn.Module):
    # Embeds each character, reads the sequence with a GRU,
    # and returns logits over the next character at every position.

    def __init__(self, embed_size=16, hidden_size=128):
        super().__init__()
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(n_chars, embed_size)
        self.recurrent = nn.GRU(embed_size, hidden_size, batch_first=True)
        self.out = nn.Linear(hidden_size, n_chars)

    def forward(self, x, state=None):
        states, state = self.recurrent(self.embed(x), state)
        return self.out(states), state


def make_lm(seed=1):
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    return CharModel()


def train_lm(net, n_steps, seed=0):
    # Adam on random windows of the training text, with gradient clipping to 1.
    # Each window's targets are the same window moved one character on.
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(net.parameters(), lr=lm_lr)
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    net.train()
    for step in range(n_steps):
        starts = torch.randint(0, n_train - seq_len - 1, (batch_size,), generator=generator)
        x = torch.stack([train_ids[s:s + seq_len] for s in starts])
        y = torch.stack([train_ids[s + 1:s + seq_len + 1] for s in starts])
        logits, _ = net(x)
        loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits.reshape(-1, n_chars), y.reshape(-1))
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        _ = nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(net.parameters(), 1)
        optimizer.step()


def lm_log_probs(net):
    # Natural log of the probability `net` gives each validation character
    # after the first, given all the validation characters before it.
    net.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits, _ = net(val_ids[:-1].unsqueeze(0))
    log_p = torch.log_softmax(logits[0], dim=1)
    return log_p[torch.arange(len(val_ids) - 1), val_ids[1:]]


def sample(net, prompt, n, temperature=1.0, seed=0):
    # Feeds `prompt`, then draws `n` characters one at a time,
    # feeding each one back in.
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    x = torch.tensor([[index[ch] for ch in prompt]])
    drawn = []
    net.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits, state = net(x)
        for _ in range(n):
            p = torch.softmax(logits[0, -1] / temperature, dim=0)
            nxt = torch.multinomial(p, 1, generator=generator)
            drawn.append(nxt.item())
            logits, state = net(nxt.view(1, 1), state)
    return prompt + decode(torch.tensor(drawn))


print(n_chars, len(text))
print(text[:120])
```

The exercises use the first `r format(nchar(py$text), big.mark = ",")` characters of the "tiny Shakespeare" text,
which @karpathy2015charrnn collected from Shakespeare's plays;
this slice is the opening of *Coriolanus*.
It has `r py$n_chars` distinct characters,
counting capitals, punctuation, the space and the line break separately.
`ids` numbers each character by its place in the sorted list `chars`.
The first `r format(py$n_train, big.mark = ",")` characters are for training,
and the remaining `r format(nchar(py$text) - py$n_train, big.mark = ",")` for validation.

`CharModel` reads a sequence of character indices with an [embedding layer](rnns.qmd#def-embedding) and a [GRU](rnns.qmd#def-gru) layer,
and maps the [hidden state](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-hidden-state) at each position to [logits](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-logits) over the next character.
`train_lm()` runs [Adam](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-adam) with [learning rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate) `r py$lm_lr` on batches of `r py$batch_size` windows of `r py$seq_len` characters,
with [gradient clipping](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html#def-gradient-clipping) to 1.
`lm_log_probs()` returns the log of the probability the network gives each validation character,
given the ones before it,
and `sample()` draws new text from the network one character at a time.
